## S3.3 Functional GEE {#sec-s4-fgee}

```{r s5-setup}
s5_read <- \(f) readr::read_csv(file.path("competitors/fgee/summaries", f), show_col_types = FALSE)
s5_A <- s5_read("A-pooled.csv")
s5_As <- s5_read("A-summary.csv")
s5_B <- s5_read("B-summary.csv") |> mutate(dep = error != "iid")
s5_BP <- s5_read("B-paired-ncv-summary.csv") |> mutate(dep = error != "iid")
s5_P <- bind_rows(s5_read("P-summary.csv"), s5_read("cardio/P-summary.csv"))
s5_PP <- bind_rows(s5_read("P-paired-ncv-summary.csv"), s5_read("cardio/Pc-paired-ncv-summary.csv"))
s5_P_ALL <- c(running = 90, dti = 92, gait_vc = 138, ecg_roahd = 100, ecg_gls4b = 78, af = 118)

# Experiment A: pooled coverage over the three coefficient functions
s5_a <- \(m, ni = c(1, 5), n = c(25, 100, 500), fam = c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial"))
  s5_A$coverage[s5_A$method %in% m & s5_A$n_i %in% ni & s5_A$N %in% n & s5_A$family %in% fam]
s5_as <- \(m, est, col, n = c(25, 100, 500)) s5_As[[col]][s5_As$method %in% m & s5_As$estimand %in% est & s5_As$N %in% n]
s5_conv <- s5_A |>
  filter(method %in% c("fgee_base_fixed", "refund_cr_freq_centred")) |>
  select(cell, family, method, coverage) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = coverage) |>
  mutate(d = abs(fgee_base_fixed - refund_cr_freq_centred))
s5_cl2_low <- s5_As |> filter(method == "refund_cl2") |> slice_min(coverage, n = 1)

# Experiment B
s5_b <- \(m, est, dep, col = "coverage") s5_B[[col]][s5_B$method %in% m & s5_B$estimand %in% est & s5_B$dep %in% dep]
s5_bp <- \(ct, e, d) s5_BP |> filter(contrast == .env$ct, estimand %in% .env$e, dep %in% .env$d)

# Plasmode
s5_p <- \(m, est, col = "coverage", apps = names(s5_P_ALL)) s5_P[[col]][s5_P$method %in% m & s5_P$estimand %in% est & s5_P$app %in% apps]
s5_pp <- \(ct, e) s5_PP |> filter(contrast == .env$ct, estimand %in% .env$e)

s5_labels <- c(
  reml_model = "REML, model-based",
  reml_cl2 = "REML + CL2",
  fgee_independent = "fGEE, independence",
  fgee_ar1 = "fGEE, AR(1)",
  fgee_fpca = "fGEE, FPCA",
  fgee_independent_wild = "fGEE, independence, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_ar1_wild = "fGEE, AR(1), calibrated crit.",
  fgee_fpca_wild = "fGEE, FPCA, calibrated crit."
)
s5_estimands <- c(beta = "β(s,t)", mean = "mean (link)", alpha = "α(t)", gamma = "γ(t)")
s5_apps <- c(ecg_gls4b = "ECG strain", af = "AF trial", running = "running", dti = "DTI",
  gait_vc = "gait", ecg_roahd = "ECG 8-lead")
```

### Their simulation design

We reran the function-on-scalar simulation of @LoewingerLevisCuiPereira2025 [Section 4] with
their data generator unchanged: $Y_{ij}(s) = \beta_0(s) + X_{1i}\beta_1(s) + X_{2i}\beta_2(s) + \varepsilon_{ij}(s)$
on 50 grid points, with Gaussian errors (variance 10) or Poisson and binary responses generated
through a Gaussian copula whose latent correlation is AR(1) (0.75) along $s$ and exchangeable
(0.75) between the curves of a subject. The design crosses the three families with
`r knitr::combine_words(sort(unique(s5_A$N)), and = " or ")` subjects and
`r paste(sort(unique(s5_A$n_i), decreasing = TRUE), collapse = " or ")` curves per subject
(`r max(s5_A$n_i)` as in their study, `r min(s5_A$n_i)` as in ours), with
`r max(s5_A$R)` replicates per setting; `r plural(sum(s5_A$R < max(s5_A$R) & !grepl("_wild$", s5_A$method)), "one-step fit")` failed
(singular system). The initial fit is their pffr call (bam with fREML,
discretisation, P-spline bases with 16 functions); all intervals labelled "initial fit" in
@tbl-s4-fgee-a are computed on that fit, the REML row on a refit of the same model and bases by gam
with REML, and all clusters are subjects. Every interval is scored through
one evaluation matrix per coefficient function; these matrices reproduce fastFGEE's fitted curves
and standard errors, so centring and basis differences between methods do not enter. As in their
Table 3, coverage is the pointwise 95% coverage averaged over the grid, over replicates and over
$\beta_0$, $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$; its Monte Carlo standard error is at most
`r f(max(s5_A$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-a
#| tbl-cap: "Their simulation design: ranges over the nine settings (three families, three numbers of subjects) of the coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals, averaged over the grid and the three coefficient functions, by number of curves per subject. Initial fit: their pffr call (bam). fGEE: one-step update with the stated functional and longitudinal working correlations. Calibrated crit.: fastFGEE's wild-bootstrap critical value with its t adjustment; z: normal critical value."
s5_a_methods <- c(
  model = "Initial fit, model-based",
  fgee_base = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, z",
  fgee_base_wild = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_base_fixed = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, penalty rescaled, z",
  refund_cr_freq_centred = "Initial fit, cluster sandwich, frequentist, centred scores",
  refund_cr = "Initial fit, CR1",
  refund_cl2 = "Initial fit, CL2",
  reml_cl2 = "REML (gam) fit, CL2",
  fgee_independent_independent = "fGEE, independence × independence, z",
  fgee_independent_independent_wild = "fGEE, independence × independence, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_ar1_exchangeable = "fGEE, AR(1) × exchangeable, z",
  fgee_ar1_exchangeable_wild = "fGEE, AR(1) × exchangeable, calibrated crit."
)
s5_A |>
  filter(method %in% names(s5_a_methods)) |>
  group_by(method, n_i) |>
  summarise(r = rng(coverage), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_i, values_from = r) |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, names(s5_a_methods))) |>
  arrange(method) |>
  mutate(method = s5_a_methods[as.character(method)]) |>
  select(method, `5`, `1`) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Intervals", "5 curves per subject", "1 curve per subject"))
```

With `r max(s5_A$n_i)` curves per subject, CL2 clustered by subject on the initial fit covers
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", 5, c(100, 500)))` with 100 or 500 subjects and
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", 5, 25))` with 25. Refitting by gam and REML changes the pooled CL2
coverage by at most
`r f(max(abs(s5_a("refund_cl2") - s5_a("reml_cl2"))), 3)`. fastFGEE's one-step intervals with its
calibrated critical values cover `r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable_wild"), 5))`
in this design; with a normal critical value they cover
`r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable"), 5, c(25, 100)))` with
at most 100 subjects and `r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable"), 5, 500))`
with 500. The one-step estimate of $\beta_1$ has an RMSE of
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_independent_independent", "beta1", "rmse") / s5_as("refund_cl2", "beta1", "rmse"))`
(independence) and
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_ar1_exchangeable", "beta1", "rmse") / s5_as("refund_cl2", "beta1", "rmse"))`
(AR(1) × exchangeable) times that of the initial fit.

### The initial-fit sandwich and penalty-scale conventions

mgcv's smoothing parameters are on the scale of the summed log-likelihood: the penalized
estimate maximizes $\sum_{i=1}^n \ell_i(\boldsymbol\theta) - \boldsymbol\theta^\top\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\boldsymbol\theta/(2\phi)$,
with $\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda} = \sum_j \lambda_j \mathbf S_j$, $n$ clusters (subjects) and the sum over
all observations of cluster $i$ in $\ell_i$ (for the Gaussian, the residual sum of squares).
A sandwich written with averaged quantities therefore needs the bread
$$
\bar{\mathbf A} = \frac1n \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf X_i^\top \mathbf W_i \mathbf X_i + \frac{\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}}{n\phi}
= (n\,\mathbf V_p)^{-1},
$$
with $\mathbf W_i$ the Fisher weights of the main text, and
$\bar{\mathbf A}^{-1}\bar{\mathbf M}\bar{\mathbf A}^{-1}/n$ with the averaged meat $\bar{\mathbf M}$
is then the cluster sandwich $\mathbf V_p(\sum_i \mathbf U_i\mathbf U_i^\top)\mathbf V_p$ up to
degrees-of-freedom factors.

The initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE 0.2.2 (`gee.fit = FALSE`), which the simulation code of
@LoewingerLevisCuiPereira2025 calls for their pffr baseline, differs in the penalty scale: it adds
$\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$ to the averaged bread, a penalty larger by the factor $n\phi$
(for the Gaussian, approximately $n\sigma^2$). The estimate is the unchanged pffr estimate, but the
inverse bread, and with it the standard errors, shrink. In their design the ratio of mean
standard error to the empirical standard deviation of $\hat\beta_1$ is
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio"))` for this sandwich and does not improve with the
number of subjects (`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio", 25))` with 25,
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio", 500))` with 500), because the penalty-scale
difference does not vanish. With `r max(s5_A$n_i)` curves per subject its pooled coverage is
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "gaussian"))` for Gaussian,
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "poisson"))` for Poisson and
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "binomial"))` for binary responses (@tbl-s4-fgee-a); its coverage here is in
line with their Table 3 for the pffr baseline. With its wild-bootstrap critical value, which widens the
intervals instead, coverage is `r rng(s5_a("fgee_base_wild", 5, c(100, 500)))` with 100 or more
subjects.

Dividing the penalty by $n\phi$ and leaving everything else unchanged gives
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base_fixed"))` over all `r nrow(s5_conv)` settings. The rescaled sandwich then
coincides with refund's frequentist cluster sandwich (no $\mathbf V_p - \mathbf V_e$ term) with
centred cluster scores: pooled coverages `r if (max(s5_conv$d[s5_conv$family != "gaussian"]) < 5e-4) "agree to three decimals" else "differ"` in every Poisson and binary setting and differ by at most
`r f(max(s5_conv$d), 3)` in the Gaussian settings, where fastFGEE estimates the working variance per
grid point instead of using one $\sigma^2$. CL2 on the same fit covers
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = c(100, 500)))` with 100 or 500 subjects and
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = 25))` with 25; the lowest single coefficient function is
`r f(s5_cl2_low$coverage, 3)` ($\beta_`r sub("beta", "", s5_cl2_low$estimand)`$,
`r c(gaussian = "Gaussian", poisson = "Poisson", binomial = "binary")[s5_cl2_low$family]`,
`r s5_cl2_low$N` subjects, `r s5_cl2_low$n_i` curve per subject). Its gain over the rescaled sandwich at
25 subjects, `r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = 25) - s5_a("fgee_base_fixed", n = 25), 3)`, combines
uncentred scores, the $\mathbf V_p - \mathbf V_e$ term and the leverage adjustment.

### The main factorial settings of our simulation

fastFGEE was started from the REML fit of the main study in its 18 main factorial settings at the default
signal level (Gaussian, Poisson and binary responses; independent, rough stationary and smooth errors;
$G = 40$ and 100; model $\mathrm{ff}(X) + z\gamma(t)$; one curve per subject;
`r min(s5_B$R)` replicates, the main study's data sets), with curves as clusters, independent
longitudinal correlation, functional working correlation independence, AR(1) or FPCA, and the
package defaults otherwise (cluster cross-validation of the smoothing parameters, wild bootstrap).
Its interval interface covers the functional intercept and scalar-covariate effects but not
$\mathrm{ff}$ surfaces or fitted means. For $\beta(s,t)$ and the mean we therefore score Wald
intervals from its covariance with the normal critical value. For $\alpha(t)$ and $\gamma(t)$ we
also transfer its calibrated critical value for the term (wild bootstrap with $t$ adjustment) to
our evaluation points and apply it to the same estimate and standard error; the calibration on the
package's own term grid need not carry over to other points. Monte Carlo standard errors of
coverage are at most `r f(max(s5_B$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-b
#| tbl-cap: "Main factorial settings of our simulation: ranges of grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals over the 12 settings with dependent errors (rough stationary, smooth) and the 6 settings with independent errors, and the ratio SE/SD (grid average of mean standard error over the empirical SD of the estimate) under dependence. fGEE intervals: Wald intervals from its covariance, or with its transferred calibrated critical value (calibrated crit.). Mean on the link scale."
s5_B |>
  filter(method %in% names(s5_labels)) |>
  group_by(estimand, method) |>
  summarise(
    cov_dep = rng(coverage[dep]),
    cov_iid = rng(coverage[!dep]),
    sesd_dep = if (grepl("_wild$", method[1])) "" else rng(se_sd_ratio[dep]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = factor(estimand, names(s5_estimands)),
    method = factor(method, names(s5_labels))
  ) |>
  arrange(estimand, method) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    method = s5_labels[as.character(method)]
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
    linesep = "", col.names = c("Estimand", "Intervals", "Cov. dependent", "Cov. independent", "SE/SD dependent"))
```

The Wald intervals for $\beta$ and the mean use the sandwich covariance fastFGEE 0.2.2 returns for
its one-step estimate under the stated working correlation. These surface results therefore do not
test fastFGEE's calibrated bootstrap procedure, which it provides only for intercepts and scalar-covariate effects, nor its performance in
its own function-on-scalar setting (studied above). Under dependent errors the fGEE Wald intervals
for $\beta$ cover
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE))` against
`r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE))` for REML + CL2 (@tbl-s4-fgee-b). Smoothing bias alone does not
explain the shortfall: the root mean squared bias of the fGEE surface estimate is
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE, "rel_bias"))` of its
empirical standard deviation (REML `r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE, "rel_bias"))`), while
SE/SD is `r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE, "se_sd_ratio"))`.
With calibrated critical values, the intervals for $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ cover
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_wild", "fgee_fpca_wild"), c("alpha", "gamma"), TRUE))`
under dependence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-mse
#| tbl-cap: "Main factorial settings: paired MSE ratios on identical data sets (ratio of mean squared errors over replicates, grid-averaged), ranges over settings. fGEE: independence working correlation. In brackets: number of settings whose 95% replicate-bootstrap interval lies entirely below one / entirely above one."
s5_ct <- c(fgee_ind_vs_reml = "fGEE / REML", ncv_vs_reml = "NCV / REML", fgee_ind_vs_ncv = "fGEE / NCV")
s5_BP |>
  filter(contrast %in% names(s5_ct)) |>
  group_by(estimand, dep, contrast) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    txt = sprintf("%s [%d/%d]", rng(est), sum(upper < 1), sum(lower > 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = txt) |>
  mutate(estimand = factor(estimand, names(s5_estimands))) |>
  arrange(estimand, desc(dep)) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    dep = ifelse(dep, "dependent", "independent")
  ) |>
  select(estimand, dep, n, all_of(names(s5_ct))) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Estimand", "Errors", "Settings", unname(s5_ct)))
```

Under dependent errors the one-step update reduces the MSE of $\beta$ relative to REML
(`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", TRUE)$est)`), by less than curve-blocked NCV
(`r rng(s5_bp("ncv_vs_reml", "beta", TRUE)$est)`): fGEE/NCV is
`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$est)`, with every bootstrap interval above one (lowest
lower bound `r f(min(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$lower), 2)`). Choosing, after the fact,
the working correlation with the lowest MSE in each setting gives
`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_best_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$est)`. Under independent errors fGEE/REML for
$\beta$ is `r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$est)`, above one in the settings with
$G = 40$ (`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$est[s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$G == 40])`).
For $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, fGEE/NCV is `r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", c("alpha", "gamma"), c(TRUE, FALSE))$est)`.

### Plasmode datasets

The plasmode comparison uses the six datasets with independent curves, the midpoint truth (refit at
the geometric mean of the REML and NCV smoothing parameters), the REML residual curves attached
to their own subjects with signs flipped per curve, all subjects and 40 subjects,
`r min(s5_P$R)` replicates per combination, and the plasmode study's own data sets; methods and interval
definitions are those of the main factorial settings (Gaussian responses). For the two cardiology datasets
only aggregate results are reported. Monte Carlo standard errors of coverage are at most
`r f(max(s5_P$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-p
#| tbl-cap: "Plasmode datasets (midpoint truth, REML residuals), β(s,t): grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals (Model, CL2: REML model-based and REML + CL2; Indep., AR(1), FPCA: fGEE Wald intervals from its covariance under that working correlation), and paired MSE ratios with 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals (fGEE with independence working correlation)."
s5_P |>
  filter(estimand == "beta", method %in% c("reml_model", "reml_cl2", "fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca")) |>
  select(app, G, method, coverage) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = coverage) |>
  left_join(
    s5_PP |>
      filter(estimand == "beta", contrast %in% c("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "fgee_ind_vs_ncv")) |>
      mutate(txt = sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", f(est, 2), f(lower, 2), f(upper, 2))) |>
      select(app, G, contrast, txt) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = txt),
    by = c("app", "G")
  ) |>
  mutate(app = factor(app, names(s5_apps))) |>
  arrange(app, desc(G)) |>
  mutate(
    app = ifelse(duplicated(app), "", s5_apps[as.character(app)]),
    across(c(reml_model, reml_cl2, fgee_independent, fgee_ar1, fgee_fpca), \(x) f(x, 2))
  ) |>
  select(app, G, reml_model, reml_cl2, fgee_independent, fgee_ar1, fgee_fpca, fgee_ind_vs_reml, fgee_ind_vs_ncv) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "lrrrrrrll", linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Dataset", "G", "Model", "CL2", "Indep.", "AR(1)", "FPCA", "fGEE / REML", "fGEE / NCV"))
```

Over the `r nrow(distinct(s5_P, app, G))` dataset and $G$ combinations, REML + CL2 covers $\beta$ at
`r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta"))`, the mean at `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "mean"))`, $\alpha$ at
`r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "alpha"))` and $\gamma$ at `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "gamma"))`; model-based
REML intervals cover $\beta$ at `r rng(s5_p("reml_model", "beta"))` (@tbl-s4-fgee-p). The fastFGEE 0.2.2 Wald
intervals cover $\beta$ at `r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta"))`
with SE/SD `r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", "se_sd_ratio"))`
(REML + CL2: `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta", "se_sd_ratio"))`), the mean at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "mean"))`, $\alpha$ at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "alpha"))` and $\gamma$ at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "gamma"))`, the lowest values for the
randomised treatment effect in the AF trial
(`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "gamma", apps = "af"))`). With
calibrated critical values the intervals for $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ cover
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_wild", "fgee_fpca_wild"), c("alpha", "gamma")))`.

For $\beta$, the MSE ratio fGEE/REML is `r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$est)`, below one
in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$est < 1)` of `r nrow(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta"))`
combinations, with the interval below one in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$upper < 1)`.
Against curve-blocked NCV it is worse in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$lower > 1)` combinations,
better in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper < 1)`
(`r paste(unique(s5_apps[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$app[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper < 1]]), collapse = ", ")`)
and not resolved in the remaining
`r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$lower <= 1 & s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper >= 1)`;
the best working correlation per combination, chosen after the fact, gives fGEE/NCV
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_best_vs_ncv", "beta")$est)`. For $\gamma$, fGEE/NCV is
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$est)`, with the interval below one in
`r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$upper < 1)` combinations
(`r knitr::combine_words(unique(s5_apps[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$app[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$upper < 1]]))`)
and above one in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$lower > 1)`; for $\alpha$ it is
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "alpha")$est)`.
